column1: # vpnhide control/stats protocol — golden vectors (docs/protocol.md §8 Layer 1).
# Language-independent. The C host test (test_protocol.c) runs these; the
# Rust (zygisk) and Kotlin (app) ports will run the SAME file, so a divergence
# on any covered corner is caught in CI. The spec is the arbiter; a vector only
# encodes what the spec already decided.
# Pipe-delimited columns. In payload/expected fields these escapes are decoded:
# liberal-in hex case (struct holds the value; lowercase-out is a format test)
# bare hex only in v2 control: a 0x-prefixed uid is malformed inside a group,
# and a malformed uid desyncs the end count -> reject whole
# u32 width overflow -> malformed uid -> reject whole (not wrap/saturate)
# duplicate uid -> last wins; output is sorted by uid, so position is not a
# unknown first token -> skip the line, payload still valid
# malformed debug flag -> skip (debug stays unchanged)
# whitespace runs collapse; tab as separator
# trailing newline optional on the last record
# non-ASCII byte -> reject just that line (its uids never reach the end count)
# non-ASCII byte as the FIRST significant line -> reject whole. It is significant
# (not blank/comment), so per §4.2 it must be the header; a non-ASCII line is not
# a valid header, so the payload is rejected rather than skipped to the next line.
# --- end fuse: a truncated payload must fail closed (v2) --------------------
# The KPM copies a config through a fixed 1024-byte buffer and truncates it
# silently, so a missing or short `end` is how that surfaces. Reject whole:
# applying a partial target set is the failure this record exists to stop.
# a malformed count leaves an earlier `end` standing (skip, like any other
# duplicates count once against the ceiling but twice against `end`
# absent -> 0, which makes `targets` the set to act on (today's blacklist)
# non-zero -> every uid not listed carries this mask, `targets` is the exception
# list. The wire carries the mechanism whether or not a producer emits it.
# malformed default -> skip the record, stays 0
# --- output is uid-sorted regardless of grouping order (v2) -----------------
# Sorted-on-parse is a contract: it is what lets a backend binary-search the
# array on every hooked call, so the parsed form cannot depend on group order.
# The version fuse is PER PROTOCOL, so the same number passes on one kind and
# fails on the other: control is at 2, telemetry at 1.
# The version token is DIGITS ONLY (§4.2). A leading `+` is not a digit, so the
# header is rejected whole — even though `+1`/`+2` name a current version. This
# pins a classic silent-drift corner: C/Rust reject `+`, but a naive decimal
# parse (e.g. Kotlin's toIntOrNull) would fold `+2` to 2 and misclassify it.
# non-ASCII first significant line rejects the whole payload — the parser must
# NOT skip it and find the header on the following line (§4.2 parity).
# fits exactly -> returned whole, ends in \n (complete)
# truncate on a line boundary; trailing \n dropped to signal incompleteness
# not even the first line fits -> empty
# Status consumer parity. ? preserves absent fields; activation requires completeness.

status_fields|vpnhide 1 status
backend 0x4 # inline comments are not supported
kver 0x0
hooks 0x0
error 0x0|?,0,0,0
